subject: English
topic: Active and passive voice III — mixed tiers
description: Active-passive transformations across tenses, modals, infinitive, gerund constructions

questions.stem: Convert to passive voice: 'The chef prepares a special dish every Sunday.'

options.option_text: A special dish was prepared by the chef on Sunday
A special dish is prepared by the chef every Sunday
Every Sunday a special dish prepares the chef
The chef has been preparing a special dish on Sunday

questions.explanation: Simple present active → simple present passive: subject + is/are + V3 + by + agent. 'A special dish IS PREPARED by the chef every Sunday.' Distractor 1 — past tense, wrong. Distractor 3 — word order is wrong (object becomes subject). Distractor 4 — present perfect continuous, changes the original tense.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Active and passive voice III — mixed tiers

questions.stem: Convert to passive voice: 'They will complete the project by next month.'

options.option_text: The project is completed by them by next month
The project will be completed by them by next month
By next month the project will complete by them
The project would have been completed by them

questions.explanation: Simple future active → simple future passive: will/shall + be + V3. 'will be completed.' Distractor 1 changes the tense to present. Distractor 3 mangles the syntax. Distractor 4 uses 'would have been' (past conditional perfect) which changes the meaning.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Active and passive voice III — mixed tiers

questions.stem: Convert to passive voice: 'Someone has stolen my bicycle from the parking lot.'

options.option_text: My bicycle was stolen by someone from the parking lot
My bicycle has been stolen from the parking lot
My bicycle is being stolen by someone from the parking
Someone is stolen by my bicycle in the parking lot

questions.explanation: Present perfect active 'has stolen' → present perfect passive: 'has been stolen'. Agent 'someone' is indefinite — typically dropped in passive (English convention: drop unknown / unimportant agents). Distractor 1 uses simple past instead of present perfect. Distractor 3 uses present continuous — wrong tense. Distractor 4 has subject-object inversion error.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Active and passive voice III — mixed tiers

questions.stem: Convert to passive voice: 'They are building a new metro line in the city.'

options.option_text: A new metro line is built by them in the city
A new metro line is being built in the city
A new metro line was being built in the city
They are being built by a new metro in the city

questions.explanation: Present continuous active 'are building' → present continuous passive: 'is/are being + V3' → 'is being built'. Indefinite 'they' often dropped in passive. Distractor 1 uses simple present (loses the ongoing sense). Distractor 3 shifts to past continuous. Distractor 4 swaps subject and object.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Active and passive voice III — mixed tiers

questions.stem: Convert to passive voice: 'You should respect your elders at all times.'

options.option_text: Your elders should be respected by you at all times
Your elders should respect you at all times
Your elders are to be respected at all times
Your elders are respecting you at all times

questions.explanation: Modal active 'should respect' → modal passive: 'should be + V3' → 'should be respected'. Distractor 2 reverses subject-object → meaning flipped. Distractor 3 uses 'are to be' (different modal sense — obligation rather than recommendation). Distractor 4 is present continuous, wrong tense.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Active and passive voice III — mixed tiers

questions.stem: Convert to active voice: 'A beautiful song was being sung by her at the concert.'

options.option_text: She sang a beautiful song at the concert
She was singing a beautiful song at the concert
She has been singing a beautiful song at the concert
She sings a beautiful song at the concert

questions.explanation: Past continuous passive 'was being sung' → past continuous active: 'was singing'. Distractor 1 uses simple past — loses the continuous aspect. Distractor 3 uses present perfect continuous. Distractor 4 uses simple present.
questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Active and passive voice III — mixed tiers

questions.stem: Convert to passive voice: 'Did the gardener water all the plants this morning?'

options.option_text: Were all the plants watered this morning by the gardener?
Did all the plants be watered this morning by the gardener?
Have all the plants been watered this morning by the gardener?
Was watering all the plants done this morning by the gardener?

questions.explanation: Past simple interrogative active 'Did the gardener water' → past simple passive interrogative: 'Were the plants watered by the gardener?'. Distractor 2 ungrammatical (you don't say 'Did + be + V3'). Distractor 3 changes tense to present perfect. Distractor 4 uses gerund construction, ungainly and wrong tense.

questions.topic: Active and passive voice III — mixed tiers

questions.stem: Which of the following sentences is written in the passive voice?

options.option_text: The jury announced its verdict after three days of deliberation.
All the jurors reached a unanimous decision within three hours.
The verdict was announced by the jury after three days of deliberation.
The judge dismissed the case citing a complete lack of evidence.

questions.explanation: C is correct because it follows the passive structure 'subject + was/were + past participle + by + agent'. Options A, B, and D all follow active voice structure where the doer directly performs the action, with no 'be' auxiliary before the past participle.

questions.stem: Choose the correct passive voice form of: 'The officer did not sign the document before the deadline.'

options.option_text: The document had not been signed by the officer before the deadline.
The document was not signed by the officer before the deadline.
The document is not signed by the officer before the deadline.
The document was not being signed by the officer before the deadline.

questions.explanation: B is correct. The original is Simple Past tense ('did not sign'), so the passive requires 'was/were + not + past participle'. Option A wrongly shifts to Past Perfect ('had not been signed'). Option C uses Simple Present ('is not signed'), changing the tense. Option D uses Past Continuous passive ('was not being signed'), which alters the meaning entirely.

questions.stem: Identify the correct passive transformation of: 'People generally consider Mahatma Gandhi to be the Father of the Nation.'

options.option_text: Mahatma Gandhi is generally considered to be the Father of the Nation.
Mahatma Gandhi has generally been considered the Father of the Nation.
The Father of the Nation is generally considered to be Mahatma Gandhi.
Mahatma Gandhi is generally being considered the Father of the Nation.

questions.explanation: A is correct. When the active subject is a generic group ('people'), it is dropped in the passive. The infinitive 'to be' is retained after 'considered'. Option B shifts to Present Perfect without justification. Option C promotes the complement ('Father of the Nation') to subject, distorting the original meaning. Option D uses the continuous form 'being considered', which is incorrect for stative verbs like 'consider'.

questions.stem: 'The coach awarded the best player the trophy at the closing ceremony.' Which passive form correctly uses the DIRECT OBJECT as the new subject?

options.option_text: The best player was awarded the trophy by the coach at the closing ceremony.
The trophy was awarded to the best player by the coach at the closing ceremony.
The trophy was being awarded to the best player by the coach at the ceremony.
The best player had been awarded the trophy by the coach at the ceremony.

questions.explanation: In the original, 'the trophy' is the direct object and 'the best player' is the indirect object. B correctly promotes the direct object to subject and re-inserts the indirect object with 'to'. Option A uses the indirect object as subject instead. Option C introduces an unjustified continuous tense. Option D shifts to Past Perfect and also uses the indirect object as subject.

questions.stem: Choose the correct passive voice form of: 'The rescue team must have reached the stranded hikers by dawn.'

options.option_text: The stranded hikers must be reached by the rescue team by dawn.
The stranded hikers must have been reached by the rescue team by dawn.
The stranded hikers should have been reached by the rescue team by dawn.
The stranded hikers had to be reached by the rescue team by dawn.

questions.explanation: B is correct. The modal perfect 'must have + past participle' in active voice becomes 'must have been + past participle' in passive. Option A drops the perfect aspect, using only 'must be'. Option C changes the modal from 'must' to 'should', altering the degree of certainty. Option D replaces 'must have' with 'had to be', shifting the meaning from logical deduction to obligation.

questions.stem: Four sentences are given. Identify the one with an INCORRECTLY formed passive voice construction.

options.option_text: The old monument was demolished by the civic authority last month.
The national award was being conferred upon the scientist at the ceremony.
The guests were arrived at the venue well before the scheduled time.
A significant chapter was opened in the history of the organisation.

questions.explanation: C is incorrect because 'arrive' is an intransitive verb — it takes no object, so it cannot be passivised. 'The guests were arrived' is ungrammatical; the correct form is simply 'The guests arrived'. Options A, B, and D all use transitive verbs ('demolish', 'confer upon', 'open') in grammatically valid passive constructions.

questions.stem: Choose the correct passive transformation of: 'The director let the assistant handle the entire project independently.'

options.option_text: The assistant was let to handle the entire project independently by the director.
The entire project was handled independently by the assistant, not the director.
The assistant was allowed to handle the entire project independently by the director.
The entire project was being independently handled by the assistant for the director.

questions.explanation: C is correct. The causative verb 'let + bare infinitive' does not passivise as 'was let to' — that construction is non-standard. Instead, it is converted to 'was/were allowed + to-infinitive'. Option A commits the common error of writing 'was let to', which is unacceptable in standard English. Option B introduces a contrast ('not the director') absent in the original. Option D switches to a continuous passive and uses 'for' instead of 'by', misrepresenting the agent relationship.
